ds: Operators promise unusually high or guaranteed returns, paying earlier investors from new deposits or recruitment fees rather than genuine profits. Collapse leaves many victims and often a trail of commingled funds and layered transfers.

src.t: FATF, guidance on risk-based approach and proceeds of fraud (general)
IOSCO, investor alerts on unregistered investment offerings (general)
ACFE, Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations (2024)

cn.rt: Victims send savings, including broken term deposits, to scheme operators; operators and mules receive in everyday accounts.

rat: Investor deposits to operators; crypto and securities variants.

ind.n: Promised returns far above market with low stated risk
ind.cx: Operator marketing guarantees consistently high returns, often with testimonials and urgency; victims relay these claims when transferring.
ind.fp: Genuine high-risk, high-return products clearly disclosed.
ind.ds: Operator marketing guarantees consistently high returns, often with testimonials and urgency; victims relay these claims when transferring.

ind.n: Many small inflows from unrelated individuals into one account
ind.cx: Operator-side: numerous retail credits referencing the 'investment' or a referral code, inconsistent with the stated business.
ind.fp: Crowdfunding, clubs or bonafide pooled schemes.
ind.ds: Numerous unrelated payers send frequent, often small, payments to one account, wallet or beneficiary, or one funder pays many beneficiaries, with no clear commercial relationship.
ind.cn: Many unrelated senders paying a single account or recipient

ind.n: Outflows paying earlier investors in matching round amounts
ind.cx: Operator-side: credits are followed by payments to prior investors in neat sums, plus cash-outs to insiders.
ind.ds: Operator-side: credits are followed by payments to prior investors in neat sums, plus cash-outs to insiders.

ind.cx: Payments reward introducing new participants rather than selling goods or services.
ind.fp: Standard multi-level marketing with genuine retail sales.
ind.ds: Payments reward introducing new participants rather than selling goods or services.

ind.cx: Operator is absent from regulator registers or holds a licence unrelated to the activity offered.
ind.ds: Payments go to operators, platforms or merchants that are absent from regulatory registers, imitate a legitimate firm, or process under a disguised merchant category.
ind.cn: Unlicensed or cloned operator receiving payments

ind.n: Delays or fees when investors request withdrawals
ind.cx: Victim-side: customers report blocked withdrawals or demands for charges and taxes; complaints rise.
ind.ds: customers report blocked withdrawals or demands for charges and taxes; complaints rise.

ind.n: Investor funds diverted to personal assets or luxury spending
ind.cx: Operator-side: lifestyle spending, property or vehicle purchases funded from investor accounts.
ind.ds: Operator-side: lifestyle spending, property or vehicle purchases funded from investor accounts.

ind.n: Customer borrowing to invest or reinvesting returns repeatedly
ind.cx: Victim-side: customer takes credit or rolls over supposed profits and refers friends.
ind.ds: customer takes credit or rolls over supposed profits and refers friends.

ind.n: Operator accounts opened in many names or institutions
ind.cx: Accounts are repeatedly opened and closed under front companies to receive deposits.
ind.ds: Accounts are repeatedly opened and closed under front companies to receive deposits.

ctl.ds: Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.
Monitors for spoofed domains, fake apps, adverts, numbers and fraudulent campaigns, and arranges takedown, suspension and customer alerts. It removes criminal infrastructure.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.
